name: Reconcile bank payments with open invoices using GPT-4o-mini, Google Sheets, Gmail and Telegram

parameters.content:
## Reconcile bank payments with open invoices using GPT-4o-mini, Google Sheets, Gmail and Telegram

### How it works

Every morning the workflow reads new payments from a "Bank" tab (paste your bank export there) and the open invoices from an "Invoices" tab. A Merge node joins them on the invoice number found in the payment description, so clean payments are matched without AI. The rest go to GPT-4o-mini with the list of open invoices; it names the best candidate with a confidence score and only matches at 80% or more are applied. A Switch classifies each match as Paid, Partial or Overpaid, updates both sheets, logs the decision and pings Telegram about anything that is not a clean full payment. Doubtful or failed AI calls land in a review queue instead of touching your books. Every Monday an aging report of overdue invoices goes out by Gmail.

### Setup steps

- Create a Google Sheet with the tabs Invoices, Bank and Log (columns in the section notes) and paste its ID into the Sheets nodes.
- Connect Google Sheets, Gmail, OpenAI and Telegram; set your chat ID and finance email.
- If your invoice numbers do not look like INV-1042, edit the regex in "Set Payment Fields".

### Customization

Change the 80% threshold in the IF node, the Paid tolerance in the Switch, or swap Telegram for Slack.

## 1. Load payments and invoices

Every morning both tabs are read at once. Payments: rows with an empty Status and a positive amount, with the invoice number pulled out of the description by a regex. Invoices: everything not yet Paid or Overpaid that still has an outstanding amount.
Bank columns: Date, Description, Counterparty, Amount, Currency, Status, MatchedInvoice, MatchNote. Invoice columns: InvoiceNumber, ClientName, ClientEmail, Amount, Currency, DueDate, Status, PaidAmount, PaidDate, MatchNote.

## 2. Match by invoice number

The Merge node adds the invoice fields to every payment whose reference matches an open invoice (left join), and the IF sends those straight to the classification step: deterministic, free and instant. Payments without a match continue to the AI step, together with the full list of open invoices collected by the Aggregate node.

## 3. Match the rest with AI

GPT-4o-mini sees one payment and all open invoices and answers in a fixed JSON shape.
The Code node looks that invoice up in the list, so the model can never invent one.
Below 80% confidence, or on any API error, the payment goes to the review queue.

## 4. Classify and record

The Switch compares the payment with the outstanding amount: Paid (within 0.01), Partial or Overpaid. The three branches meet again and then update the invoice row, mark the bank row and append a line to the Log tab. Anything that is not a clean full payment is sent to Telegram.

## Review queue: nothing is guessed

Unmatched payments are marked "Review" in the Bank tab
with the AI's best guess and reasoning, logged, and sent
to Telegram for a human decision.
Invoices are never touched from this branch.

## 5. Weekly aging report

Every Monday the open invoices are read again, overdue ones are bucketed (1-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+ days) and a sorted HTML table with totals per currency is emailed via Gmail.

### 🚀 Want this wired into your accounting stack?

This template is the safe starting point. I build extended versions for real businesses: **QuickBooks, Xero or Stripe** instead of a spreadsheet, live **bank feeds** (GoCardless, Plaid) instead of CSV pastes, one payment covering several invoices, **customer statements** and dunning, Slack instead of Telegram.

Async delivery, no calls - contact links in my creator profile.

options.systemMessage:
You reconcile incoming bank payments against open customer invoices for a small business. You receive ONE bank transaction and the list of currently open invoices. Decide which single invoice this payment most likely settles.

Signals, strongest first:
1. An invoice number (or its digits) in the description or reference, even with typos, a missing prefix or extra spaces.
2. The counterparty name matching the customer name (company names are often abbreviated, in a different case or without the legal suffix).
3. The amount equal to the outstanding amount of exactly one open invoice, or to the sum of several invoices of the same customer.

Rules:
- Use ONLY the data provided. Never invent invoice numbers: invoice_id must be copied exactly from the list, or be an empty string.
- Currencies must match unless the description clearly explains a conversion.
- If one payment plausibly covers several invoices of the same customer, pick the oldest one and say so in the reasoning.
- match_type: "exact" when the amount equals the outstanding amount (within 0.01), "partial" when it is lower, "overpayment" when it is higher, "none" when no invoice fits.
- confidence 0-100: 90+ = invoice number or exact amount plus a matching name; 70-89 = one strong signal; below 70 = weak or conflicting signals. Anything below 80 is sent to a human, so be honest rather than generous.
- Keep the reasoning to one or two sentences a bookkeeper can verify.

Return ONLY JSON that matches the schema.
